translationRepairs: Yanzhang rushed to attack, as Chongtao had foreseen. In the midsummer heat his men dropped dead; they failed to take the fort and lost more than half their strength. As they hurried back toward Yangliu, Zhuangzong met them and broke them.

Yanzhang indeed rushed to attack. In the midsummer heat his men dropped dead; they failed to take the fort and lost more than half their strength. As they hurried back toward Yangliu, Zhuangzong met them and broke them.
The sentence does not name Chongtao or ascribe foresight to him, so that clause must go; 果 still marks the attack as happening as expected and should be kept.

Chongtao grew afraid and confided in the sons of old friends: “I helped the emperor win the realm. The great work is done, and petty men are closing in. I want to withdraw to Zhenyuan and try to dodge ruin—is that wise?”

Chongtao grew afraid and confided in the sons of old friends: “I helped the emperor win the realm. The great work is done, and petty men are closing in. I want to withdraw to Zhenyang and try to dodge ruin—is that wise?”
歸守鎮陽 names Zhenyang; Zhenyuan is a wrong reading of 陽.

Chongtao grew quite afraid and told the sons of old friends: “I aided the Son of Heaven in taking the realm. Now the great work is done and petty men rise together. I wish to withdraw, return to guard Zhenyuan, and perhaps escape disaster—is that possible?”

Chongtao grew quite afraid and told the sons of old friends: “I aided the Son of Heaven in taking the realm. Now the great work is done and petty men rise together. I wish to withdraw, return to guard Zhenyang, and perhaps escape disaster—is that possible?”
歸守鎮陽 is Zhenyang, not Zhenyuan.

Chongtao memorialized again and again, asking to restore the old Tang practice of putting eunuchs back in the Privy Commission and to be released from Zhenyuan. The court answered with a gracious refusal.

Chongtao memorialized again and again, asking to restore the old Tang practice of putting eunuchs back in the Privy Commission and to be released from Zhenyang. The court answered with a gracious refusal.
並辭鎮陽 is declining Zhenyang, not Zhenyuan.

Chongtao repeatedly memorialized on his own behalf, asking to restore the Tang custom of returning the Privy Commission to inner courtiers, and at the same time declined Zhenyuan—a gracious edict would not allow it.

Chongtao repeatedly memorialized on his own behalf, asking to restore the Tang custom of returning the Privy Commission to inner courtiers, and at the same time declined Zhenyang—a gracious edict would not allow it.
並辭鎮陽 is Zhenyang, not Zhenyuan.
Quanyi was furious and sent men to Empress Liu to plead Guan’s case in soft words. Meanwhile the emperor’s attendants spent day and night picking at Guan’s every flaw.
Quanyi was furious and sent men to Empress Liu to lay out Guan’s offenses in mild words. Meanwhile the emperor’s attendants spent day and night picking at Guan’s every flaw.
After 全義大怒, 告劉皇后 and 白貫事 report Guan to the empress; they are not a plea for him.
Quanyi was greatly angered and once sent men to tell Empress Liu, gently pleading Guan’s case—but the emperor’s attendants day and night jointly attacked Guan’s faults.
Quanyi was greatly angered and once sent men to tell Empress Liu, calmly stating Guan’s offenses—but the emperor’s attendants day and night jointly attacked Guan’s faults.
白貫事, following Quanyi’s anger, states Guan’s conduct against him, not a defense of Guan.

When the army reached Chengdu, Zongbi moved Yan to the western palace and sent Yan’s concubines, entertainers, and treasures to Chongtao and his son Tinghui.
其子廷誨 is Tinghui; Yanhui misreads 廷.
